hero.description: Xalor is a build-time TypeScript engine that turns your native types into a live runtime validation and generation system — without duplicating schemas or shipping heavy libraries.

whatIsXalor.description: Xalor shifts heavy type parsing from the browser directly to your build toolchain. It compiles your native, pristine TypeScript types into lightweight, hidden blueprints—completely **eliminating production runtime overhead** and dual-source schema maintenance code loops.
whatIsXalor.subDescription: Instead of parsing graphs or reconstructing types at runtime, Xalor executes against precompiled, content-addressed structures created entirely during the build process, yielding a flat _0.8KB client bundle footprint_.

stepOne.description: Declare standard TypeScript interfaces exactly as you always do. There are **no custom validation schema domain languages** to learn, no heavy script generator utilities, and zero file-tree clutter.

stepTwo.description: Xalor's background watcher sweeps your codebase, extracts the Type AST, and flattens layouts into **pointer-interned structural snapshots** using ultra-compact Content-Addressable Storage (CAS) interning.

stepThree.description: The application boots instantly via an _O(1) memory hydration map_. Validate inbound payloads, stamp out mock test fixtures, and transform object shapes smoothly at near **hardware-level speeds**.

runtimeModule.description: Stop maintaining separate verification engines and mock data setups. Xalor converts native types into high-speed runtime systems with zero bundle inflation.

validate.description: Ensure raw inbound payloads match your compile-time types with deep error reporting and zero runtime schema overhead.
validate.subDescription: Catch structural failures instantly at your system boundaries.

generate.description: Stamp out completely populated testing fixtures, safe default fallbacks, and mock shapes derived directly from native type graphs.
generate.subDescription: Instant mockup datasets generated without maintaining fixture files.

transform.description: Pick, omit, sanitize, and reshape messy structures using type-aware utilities running on hardware-level lookup paths.
transform.subDescription: Peel away unsafe variables without redefining your schemas.

match.description: Eliminate the dual-source tax entirely. Write standard TypeScript contracts once and execute them natively anywhere across your stack.
match.subDescription: Absolute architectural sync across edge paths and user frontends.

verificationMatrix.subHeader: See how Xalor transforms pristine, native TypeScript contracts into high-speed runtime systems—completely eliminating the parsing latencies, bloated files, and boilerplate of traditional dependencies.

matrixRows.featureTitle: Pristine Native Types as Single Source of Truth
matrixRows.description: Write standard TypeScript interfaces exactly as you always do. Modifying a native type updates runtime validation mechanics on your next save loop, completely **cutting out human schema duplication errors**.
Heavy validation engines never ship to the browser. Parsing logic is completely stripped from your production build, dropping client runtime weights down to a **flat 0.8KB instance blueprint size**.

matrixRows.featureTitle: Zero Workspace Clutter (No Generated Code Files)
matrixRows.description: The compiler watcher runs entirely in memory. It leaves **zero massive, auto-generated validation function files** to clutter your local source directories or pollute your git history.

When raw incoming data boundaries crack, error logs don't print vague path trees. Xalor traces the validation fault straight back to a **fully clickable terminal link pointing to the exact source line** where your type was declared.

Stop wasting hours manually creating and updating massive static mockup `.json` fixture files. Stamp out dynamic, randomized, and structurally valid dummy datasets instantly using a **single inline generator execution**.
